# Safety, Guardrails & Security

> Guardrails, permissions, constitutions, red-teaming and security of model-driven robots.  
> Layer: L5 · 45 entries · [overview](../README.md#safety) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- ⚪ [**Verify-Adapt-Hold**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30523 "Containing Behavioral Cascades from Manipulated Claims in LLM-Powered Multi-Robot Systems") · 2026-09 — Active verification for LLM-powered robot fleets after a false world-state claim is accepted: a Verify-Adapt-Hold plan sends some robots to inspect, lets a few adapt and keeps the rest on trusted plans, containing fleet-wide replanning cascades.
- ⚪ [**ShieldVLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13231 "ShieldVLA: Feasibility-Aware Safety Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-09 — Safety-aligned VLA fine-tuning based on Hamilton-Jacobi reachability: a safety critic learned from visual observations gates policy optimization, separating reward seeking in feasible regions from recovery near unsafe states, with rubric-based VLM safety scores as supervision.
- 🟢 [**SafeLoop**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26313 "SafeLoop: Risk-Aware Rollback for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation") · 2026-09 · Nanjing University et al. — External wrapper that adds hazard prediction and rollback to a VLA without changing its weights: a risk predictor estimates probability and time-to-hazard for collisions and object failures, and a controller continues, saves a safety checkpoint or rolls back in joint space. IROS 2026. [code](https://github.com/Loule0-0/SafeLoop)
- ⚪ [**Refusals That Bend**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38971 "Refusals That Bend: Measuring and Predicting Task Malleability in Embodied VLM Planners") · 2026-09 — Shows that placing one ordinary object in the scene flips 20.2% of tasks a constitution-guarded embodied VLM planner initially refused into compliance, with no adversarial pixels or prompts, and predicts which tasks are malleable using signals from a small open VLM.
- ⚪ [**RCDH**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35039 "Do Not Cut When Uncertain: Rejectable and Calibrated Decision Heads for VLA Policies in Robotic Harvesting") · 2026-09 — Replaces a frozen VLA's output head with a typed decision schema that includes explicit rejection, plus calibration for risk-aware abstention, so the policy can decline to act under occlusion; tested on a robotic harvesting platform.
- ⚪ [**Predictive Semantic Safety**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34356 "Predictive Semantic Safety: From Visual Physical Reasoning to Safety-Critical Control") · 2026-09 — A VLM predicts physical events such as falling fixtures and their timing; conformal prediction turns them into calibrated future object occupancy, which a backup-based safety filter uses to minimally modify the robot's commands; evaluated in MuJoCo with a Unitree Go1. [project](https://www.taekyung.me/pss)
- ⚪ [**PlanGuard**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32801 "PlanGuard: A Guardrail for Multi-Step Plan Safety in Embodied Agents") · 2026-09 — Pre-execution guardrail that judges the physical safety of a complete multi-step plan in its environment, trained on the MSP-Safe dataset and distilled into a 2B model with on-policy strong-teacher distillation. _Note: Code and data announced but not yet released._
- ⚪ [**Multi-Link Safety Filter**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40007 "Multi-Link Safety Filtering for VLA Policies Around Moving Hazards") · 2026-09 — Training-free run-time shield for a pretrained VLA: five ellipsoids cover gripper, wrist and forearm, and one barrier program filters every command against a keep-out ellipsoid that sparse optical flow moves with the hazard; runs on edge CPUs alongside pi0.5 and on an SO-101 arm. [project](https://yathag.github.io/multilink-safety-filter/)
- ⚪ [**Humanoid LLM-Orchestrator Safety Benchmark**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07288 "How Long Until Your Robot Ignores You? A Safety Benchmark for LLM Orchestrators in Human-Humanoid Collaboration") · 2026-09 — MCP-based benchmark for LLMs orchestrating a humanoid, with five safety invariants grounded in ISO 10218-2:2025, a four-level compliance taxonomy (over- to under-compliance) and text, simulation and Unitree G1 evaluation layers. _Note: Only text-layer results reported so far; tests long sessions under different context-management budgets._
- ⚪ [**Physical Prompt Injection Study**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05715 "Hijacking Robots with a Piece of Paper: A Systematic Study of Physical Prompt Injection in VLM-Controlled Robots") · 2026-08 · Singapore University of Technology and Design — Tests adversarial signage in the camera view as indirect prompt injection against VLM-planned robot sorting (5,670 trials on GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3-VL-32B) and evaluates prompt defences, two-stage verification and text masking. _Note: First-party attack success of 27.0%, 29.4% and 5.0% for the three models._
- ⚪ [**Multi-Robot Communication Attacks**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06830 "When Coordination Becomes a Threat: Communication Attacks in LLM-Controlled Multi-Robot Systems") · 2026-08 — Formulates external-entry and privileged in-system communication attacks and shows unsafe messages turn into unsafe actions across decentralized and hybrid (DMAS, HMAS-1, HMAS-2) LLM multi-robot architectures.
- ⚪ [**Edge Skillguard**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25091 "Auto-Policy, not Auto-Skill: Compiled Agent Skills for the Physical World") · 2026-08 — Names 'Borrowed Authority' attacks in which malicious agent skills drive physical actuation, and proposes Edge Skillguard, a typed authority layer inside skill artifacts that decides which behaviors may become actions.
- ⚪ [**SafeRelBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14543 "SafeRelBench: A Spatial-Relation-Aware Benchmark for Process-Level Safety in VLM-Driven Embodied Agents") · 2026-07 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications — Process-level safety benchmark for VLM-driven embodied agents with 507 executable samples (248 spatial-relation, 259 controls) testing whether agents check support, containment and proximity conditions before risky actions, not just final task success.
- 🟡 [**NVIDIA Halos for Robotics**](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-halos-for-robotics-the-industrys-first-full-stack-safety-system-for-physical-ai) · 2026-06 · NVIDIA — Full-stack functional-safety system for physical AI: IGX Thor compute and Holoscan Sensor Bridge, the Halos OS safety stack (Halos Core, open-source Outside-In Safety Blueprint) and an ANAB-accredited AI Systems Inspection Lab; Agility is the lead partner. _Note: Announced at Automate 2026 (2026-06-22). Blueprint is early access; its README says it is not for production safety use without a certified safety layer._ [code](https://github.com/NVIDIA/halos-outside-in-safety) · [docs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-trust-center/halos/robotics/)
- 🟢 [**LIBERO-Safety**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23686 "LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-06 — Parametric benchmark that procedurally generates safety-critical manipulation scenarios, with a keypose-driven pipeline yielding 19,664 collision-free demonstrations and an evaluation of eight VLAs and two embodied foundation models. _Note: ECCV 2026._ [code](https://github.com/LIBERO-SAFETY/LIBERO-Safety) · [project](https://libero-safety.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LIBERO-Safety/libero_safety)
- ⚪ [**Single-Robot Compromise Propagation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15641 "Propagating Unsafe Actions in LLM Controlled Multi-Robot Collaboration via Single Robot Compromise") · 2026-05 — Attack paradigm where an adversary interacts with only one entry robot, which then spreads malicious intent over inter-robot communication, causing coordinated unsafe actions in LLM-planned multi-robot teams. IJCAI 2026.
- ⚪ [**SafeVLA-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00773 "SafeVLA-Bench: A Benchmark for the Success-Safety Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-05 · University of Pennsylvania — Post-hoc safety layer for simulator VLA benchmarks that encodes task-aware safety requirements in Signal Temporal Logic and reports succeeded-but-unsafe rates and violation severity on LIBERO and RoboCasa-365. _Note: First-party: 36-56% of successful RoboCasa-365 rollouts violate at least one safety clause. Project page hosts a leaderboard._ [project](https://safevla.org/)
- 🟢 [**Runtime governance for embodied agents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07833 "Harnessing Embodied Agents: Runtime Governance for Policy-Constrained Execution") · 2026-04 — Moves governance out of the agent loop into a runtime layer that performs policy checks, capability admission, execution monitoring, rollback and human override, evaluated in randomized simulated trials against AutoRT-style constitution filtering and other baselines. [code](https://github.com/s20sc/harnessing-embodied-agents)
- 🟢 [**HazardArena**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12447 "HazardArena: Evaluating Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-04 — VLA semantic-safety benchmark of matched safe/unsafe twin scenarios (same objects, layout and motion, different risk context), with 2,000+ assets and 51 tasks; finds safe-only fine-tuning also raises hazardous execution. [code](https://github.com/HazardArena-Team/HazardArena)
- ⚪ [**Modular Safety Guardrails (position)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04056 "Modular Safety Guardrails Are Necessary for Foundation-Model-Enabled Robots in the Real World") · 2026-02 — Position paper that splits foundation-model robot safety into action, decision and human-centred safety and argues for modular monitoring and intervention guardrail layers across the autonomy stack, with cross-layer co-design.

**2025**

- ⚪ [**RoboSafe**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21220 "RoboSafe: Safeguarding Embodied Agents via Executable Safety Logic") · 2025-12 — Runtime guardrail for VLM-driven embodied agents that keeps a long/short-term safety memory, infers temporal safety predicates from recent trajectories and forecasts upcoming risks, all as executable predicate code that triggers replanning. _Note: Code promised upon acceptance._
- 🟢 [**AEGIS (VLSA)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11891 "VLSA: Vision-Language-Action Models with Plug-and-Play Safety Constraint Layer") · 2025-12 · Tsinghua University — Adds a plug-and-play control-barrier-function safety constraint layer to existing VLAs for collision avoidance with theoretical guarantees, and introduces the SafeLIBERO benchmark of obstacle-intervention manipulation scenarios. _Note: IROS 2026. Source of the SafeLIBERO benchmark._ [code](https://github.com/THU-RCSCT/vlsa-aegis) · [project](https://vlsa-aegis.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**SHAWSHANK**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16347 "The Shawshank Redemption of Embodied AI: Understanding and Benchmarking Indirect Environmental Jailbreaks") · 2025-11 — Introduces indirect environmental jailbreaks, where instructions placed in the scene (e.g. written on a wall) hijack VLM-driven embodied agents, plus automatic attack (SHAWSHANK) and benchmark-generation (SHAWSHANK-FORGE) frameworks. _Note: Authors report compromising all six tested VLMs and responsible disclosure to vendors; no code link found._ [project](https://shawshankiej.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**Unitree G1 Security Assessment**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.14139 "Cybersecurity AI: Humanoid Robots as Attack Vectors") · 2025-09 · Alias Robotics — Security assessment of the Unitree G1 humanoid reporting a BLE provisioning command-injection flaw with hardcoded shared keys, weak proprietary encryption layers, and periodic telemetry exfiltration to remote servers without operator notice. _Note: Platform-level (non-model) attack surface of a humanoid widely used as an LLM/VLA testbed._
- 🟢 [**HomeSafeBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23690 "HomeSafeBench: Benchmarking Embodied Vision-Language Models in Free-Exploration Home Safety Inspection") · 2025-09 — Free-exploration home-safety inspection benchmark on VirtualHome: an embodied VLM agent navigates and adjusts its viewpoint to report hazards across five categories in 1,000 human-validated tasks; first-party best VLM F1 is ~35% vs 98% for humans. [code](https://github.com/BITHLP/HomeSafeBench)
- 🟡 [**ASIMOV-2.0**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21651 "Can AI Perceive Physical Danger and Intervene?") · 2025-09 · Google DeepMind — Second ASIMOV release: turns real injury narratives and operational constraints into photorealistic images and videos of safe-to-unsafe transitions for continuous physical-safety benchmarking, plus post-training for explicit safety-constraint reasoning. _Note: Data distributed via a Colab linked from the project page; post-trained models not released._ [project](https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v2/)
- 🟢 [**RoboGCG**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03350 "Adversarial Attacks on Robotic Vision Language Action Models") · 2025-06 — Adapts LLM jailbreak optimisation to VLAs and shows a single textual prompt at the start of a rollout can give an attacker full control over the action space of common VLAs, often persisting over long horizons. [code](https://github.com/eliotjones1/robogcg)
- 🟢 [**IS-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16402 "IS-Bench: Evaluating Interactive Safety of VLM-Driven Embodied Agents in Daily Household Tasks") · 2025-06 · Shanghai AI Laboratory — Interactive-safety benchmark of 161 household scenarios with 388 safety risks in a high-fidelity simulator; process-oriented evaluation checks whether mitigation steps happen before/after the risky step, not just the final outcome. [code](https://github.com/AI45Lab/IS-Bench)
- ⚪ [**AGENTSAFE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14697 "AGENTSAFE: Benchmarking the Safety of Embodied Agents on Hazardous Instructions") · 2025-06 · Beihang University et al. — Safety benchmark for VLM embodied agents: SAFE-THOR adversarial sandbox with a universal high-to-low-level adapter, SAFE-VERSE (45 scenarios, 1,350 hazardous tasks, 9,900 instructions) and SAFE-DIAGNOSE scoring perception, planning and execution. _Note: CVPR 2026; finds agents that recognize hazards still plan and execute unsafe actions. No code link found._
- ⚪ [**SHIELD**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11494 "SHIELD: Safety on Humanoids via CBFs In Expectation on Learned Dynamics") · 2025-05 — Minimally invasive safety layer for learned humanoid controllers: a generative stochastic dynamics residual trained on hardware data feeds a stochastic discrete-time control barrier function that enforces constraints in probability; shown on a Unitree G1. _Note: IROS 2025._
- ⚪ [**ISO 25785-1**](https://www.iso.org/standard/91469.html "Robotics - Safety requirements for dynamically stable industrial mobile robots (legged, wheeled, or other forms of locomotion) - Part 1: Robots") · 2025-05 · ISO/TC 299 — First ISO safety standard being written for industrial mobile robots with actively controlled stability (humanoids, quadrupeds, balancing wheeled robots), whose safe state itself requires power and active control. _Note: Under development (ISO/CD stage on iso.org). Date = public working-draft milestone announced by the A3/Agility/Boston Dynamics-led working group (May 2025). iso.org blocks automated fetches; page confirmed via search listing._
- 🟢 [**BadVLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16640 "BadVLA: Towards Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models via Objective-Decoupled Optimization") · 2025-05 — First backdoor attack on VLAs: objective-decoupled optimisation isolates trigger features so a trigger induces control deviations while clean-task performance is preserved; near-100% attack success reported on several VLA benchmarks (first-party). [code](https://github.com/Zxy-MLlab/BadVLA) · [project](https://badvla-project.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lostgreen/BadVLA)
- 🟢 [**SafeVLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03480 "SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning") · 2025-03 · Peking University — Integrated safety approach that models safety requirements, elicits unsafe behaviours and aligns VLAs with constrained RL (a CMDP min-max objective) for long-horizon mobile manipulation, with targeted safety evaluations. _Note: NeurIPS 2025 spotlight; first-party 83.58% reduction in cumulative safety cost vs. prior SOTA._ [code](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment/SafeVLA) · [project](https://pku-safevla.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RoboGuard**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07885 "Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots") · 2025-03 · University of Pennsylvania — Two-stage guardrail: a root-of-trust LLM grounds predefined safety rules in the current scene as temporal-logic specs, then control synthesis resolves conflicts with the proposed plan; unsafe plan execution fell from >92% to <3% under jailbreaks (first-party). [code](https://github.com/KumarRobotics/RoboGuard) · [project](https://robo-guard.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**ASIMOV Benchmark**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08663 "Generating Robot Constitutions & Benchmarks for Semantic Safety") · 2025-03 · Google DeepMind — Releases the ASIMOV benchmark for semantic safety of VLM robot "brains", generated from real images and hospital injury reports, and a method to auto-generate and auto-amend robot constitutions that steer behaviour via Constitutional AI. _Note: First-party top alignment rate 84.3% with generated constitutions. Constitution idea first used in AutoRT (see other)._ [code](https://github.com/asimov-benchmark/code) · [project](https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v1/)

**2024**

- 🟢 [**SafeAgentBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13178 "SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents") · 2024-12 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University — 750 executable tasks covering 10 hazard types in SafeAgentEnv (17 high-level actions), scored by execution and semantics; the most safety-conscious baseline rejected only 10% of detailed hazardous tasks (first-party). [code](https://github.com/shengyin1224/SafeAgentBench) · [project](https://safeagentbench.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/safeagentbench/SafeAgentBench)
- ⚪ [**POEF**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16633 "Easier Said Than Done: Unpacking Intent-Behavior Gap in Jailbreaking LLM-based Robots") · 2024-12 · Zhejiang University — Shows most LLM jailbreaks yield malicious-looking but non-executable robot policies and introduces POEF, automated red teaming that optimises jailbreaks under control-API and physical-feasibility constraints; tested on Unitree G1, Franka and simulators. _Note: Accepted to NDSS 2027; arXiv v1 was titled 'POEX: Policy Executable Embodied AI Jailbreak Attacks'._ [project](https://zjushine.github.io/poef.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RoboticAttack**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13587 "Exploring the Adversarial Vulnerabilities of Vision-Language-Action Models in Robotics") · 2024-11 — Systematic robustness study of VLAs with untargeted objectives that destabilise actions and a targeted trajectory-hijacking objective, realised as small adversarial patches that work in simulation and the physical world. _Note: ICCV 2025._ [code](https://github.com/William-wAng618/roboticAttack) · [project](https://vlaattacker.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**Embodied Red Teaming (ERT)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18676 "Embodied Red Teaming for Auditing Robotic Foundation Models") · 2024-11 · MIT — Automated red teaming that uses VLMs to generate diverse, contextually grounded instructions that make language-conditioned robot policies fail or act unsafely, exposing gaps left by fixed-instruction benchmarks. [code](https://github.com/Improbable-AI/embodied-red-teaming) · [project](https://s-karnik.github.io/embodied-red-team-project-page/)
- 🟢 [**RoboPAIR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13691 "Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots") · 2024-10 · University of Pennsylvania — First algorithm for jailbreaking LLM-controlled robots into harmful physical actions, shown white-box (NVIDIA Dolphins driving LLM), gray-box (Jackal UGV with GPT-4o) and black-box (Unitree Go2), the first jailbreak of a deployed commercial robot. [code](https://github.com/arobey1/robopair) · [project](https://robopair.org/)
- 🟢 [**SELP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19471 "SELP: Generating Safe and Efficient Task Plans for Robot Agents with Large Language Models") · 2024-09 · Purdue University — LLM planner that samples LTL translations of a command and keeps the majority-equivalent formula (equivalence voting), then uses it for constrained plan decoding plus domain fine-tuning; evaluated on drone navigation and manipulation. _Note: ICRA 2025._ [code](https://github.com/lt-asset/selp)
- 🟢 [**EARBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04449 "EARBench: Towards Evaluating Physical Risk Awareness for Task Planning of Foundation Model-based Embodied AI Agents") · 2024-08 — Multi-agent framework that generates safety guidelines and risk-prone text/visual scenarios and scores the physical risk of plans from foundation-model agents; evaluated models had a 95.75% average task risk rate (first-party). [code](https://github.com/zihao-ai/EARBench)
- 🟢 [**BadRobot**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20242 "BadRobot: Jailbreaking Embodied LLM Agents in the Physical World") · 2024-07 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology — Voice-based attack paradigm that makes embodied LLM agents violate safety and ethical constraints by exploiting jailbroken LLMs, language-action misalignment and world-knowledge flaws; benchmarked on VoxPoser, Code as Policies and ProgPrompt. _Note: ICLR 2025._ [code](https://github.com/ZhangHangTao/BadRobot) · [project](https://embodied-llms-safety.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**LLM Robot Harms Audit**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08824 "LLM-Driven Robots Risk Enacting Discrimination, Violence, and Unlawful Actions") · 2024-06 · King's College London, Carnegie Mellon University — HRI-focused audit showing that popular LLMs produce directly discriminatory outputs across protected characteristics and accept dangerous, violent or unlawful open-vocabulary instructions when used for robot tasks. _Note: Published in the International Journal of Social Robotics (2025)._ [code](https://github.com/rumaisa-azeem/llm-robots-discrimination-safety)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**Safety Chip**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09919 "Plug in the Safety Chip: Enforcing Constraints for LLM-driven Robot Agents") · 2023-09 · Brown University — Queryable safety-constraint module that translates natural-language rules into linear temporal logic, explains violations and prunes unsafe actions proposed by an LLM agent; tested in VirtualHome and on a real robot. [code](https://github.com/YzyLmc/ltl_safety) · [project](https://yzylmc.github.io/safety-chip/)
